shared_config.policy: Portable and Linux Ghostty keys retain upstream names and semantics.

scope.toolkit_mapping_policy: GTK-prefixed settings remain GTK-only; meaningful Qt equivalents use independently designed ghostty-qt frontend settings.

status_definitions.supported: Upstream-compatible behavior is implemented and tested.
status_definitions.partial: Some behavior exists, but the upstream interface or semantics are incomplete.
status_definitions.planned: The item is in scope but is not implemented yet.
status_definitions.blocked_upstream: Implementation requires a missing stable libghostty-vt capability.
status_definitions.not_applicable: The item is outside the Linux/Wayland/Qt parity target.

scope_definitions.linux: Linux behavior independent of the display server.
scope_definitions.qt_mapping: GTK-facing behavior with a meaningful Qt equivalent.
scope_definitions.gtk_only: GTK implementation detail without a Qt parity requirement.

abnormal-command-exit-runtime.note: The exact finalized u32 millisecond threshold defaults to 250 and applies live. A nonzero or signaled child observed at or before the inclusive threshold remains open with a bottom Qt failure banner and Close action; pidfd readiness minimizes Linux exit-observation latency with the existing poller as fallback, and the clock is frozen before final PTY drain/render work. Child-side lookup and execve failures participate as 126/127. Terminal-encoded input dismisses non-held abnormal exits independently of wait-after-command, while the frontend-only initial --hold remains indefinite.

adjust-box-thickness.note: Exact behavior depends on Ghostty's private generated-box sprite and font-classification pipeline, which is not exposed through public libghostty-vt.

adjust-cell-height.note: Absolute and percentage modifiers apply to the regular-face cell height in rounded physical pixels at the pane's current DPR. The pinned sparse-map application order is preserved, including its dependent baseline and decoration recentering, while cursor height keeps its independent basis.

adjust-cell-width.note: Absolute and percentage modifiers apply to the regular-face cell advance in rounded physical pixels at the pane's current DPR and drive both rendering geometry and PTY columns.

adjust-cursor-height.note: The modifier applies in rounded physical pixels to the unadjusted cell-height basis, clamps only to a one-pixel minimum, and vertically centers the result; a configured full cursor may intentionally exceed the cell.

adjust-cursor-thickness.note: The modifier applies to Ghostty's one-physical-pixel cursor-stroke basis and controls bar, underline, and hollow cursor strokes.

adjust-font-baseline.note: The signed baseline modifier applies in rounded physical pixels in Ghostty's pinned sparse-map order and updates glyph placement live.

adjust-icon-height.note: Exact behavior depends on Ghostty's private icon and Nerd Font glyph-classification pipeline, which is not exposed through public libghostty-vt.

adjust-overline-position.note: The signed position modifier applies in rounded physical pixels in Ghostty's pinned sparse-map order; negative positions remain representable for Ghostty-compatible placement.

adjust-overline-thickness.note: The modifier applies in rounded physical pixels to the regular-face line thickness and drives rendered overline geometry.

adjust-strikethrough-position.note: The unsigned position modifier applies in rounded physical pixels in Ghostty's pinned sparse-map order, saturates at zero, and drives rendered strike-through geometry.

adjust-strikethrough-thickness.note: The modifier applies in rounded physical pixels to the regular-face line thickness and drives rendered strike-through geometry.

adjust-underline-position.note: The unsigned position modifier applies in rounded physical pixels in Ghostty's pinned sparse-map order, saturates at zero, and drives single, double, curly, dotted, and dashed underline placement.

adjust-underline-thickness.note: The modifier applies in rounded physical pixels to the regular-face underline thickness and drives every rendered underline style.

alpha-blending.note: Qt Quick currently owns text and primitive blending and does not expose Ghostty's exact native, linear, and linear-corrected renderer pipeline, including the Linux linear-corrected default. Background opacity is implemented independently and does not claim this color-space behavior.

app-notifications.note: The exact clipboard-copy and config-reload flags drive a bounded FIFO toast queue owned independently by every Qt window. Successful standard-clipboard text and MIME commits distinguish copied from cleared content, while primary-only writes remain silent; successful post-startup configuration generations notify every retained window. Both policies reload live without recreating windows or panes, and the input-transparent presentation restarts its three-second timer for each queued item. This remains separate from native desktop notifications.

background.note: The exact pinned parser supplies the color and the libghostty adapter applies it to new and existing panes.

background-blur.note: The strict config wire preserves Ghostty's exact finalized i16 C value: false and zero disable, true maps to 20, explicit radii retain 0 through 255, and both negative macOS glass sentinels remain distinct. Normal and quick-terminal windows apply every nonzero value as KWin's whole-client BlurBehind request through the optional KF6 WindowSystem backend, after native surface creation and across live reload or surface recreation without touching panes, workers, terminals, or PTYs. KWin exposes only a boolean, so it ignores the retained radius; builds without KF6 WindowSystem, other Wayland compositors, and sessions where KWin does not advertise blur are deterministic no-ops.

background-image.note: The pinned optional Path is exported as a finalized absolute path with required/optional provenance. Each pane asynchronously decodes only PNG or JPEG without EXIF auto-rotation, keeps its prior image until a changed path succeeds, unloads on null, and logs while retaining the prior asset on failure; reload does not reread its unchanged source or retry that pane's failed source. Identical concurrent work coalesces through a weak process-wide metadata-keyed cache of packed straight-alpha RGBA8 images, with a bounded 250 ms failure throttle, while every split owns independent full-surface placement, texture, and composition state. Explicit raw RHI upload preserves straight-alpha filtering and shader-time premultiplication with one four-byte-per-pixel CPU image and one four-byte-per-pixel GPU texture. Shader reflection, upload telemetry, and OpenGL/Vulkan semantic integration cover that contract. The software scene-graph fallback remains an explicitly documented source-resolution approximation, and final real-Wayland compositor presentation remains interactive validation.

background-image-fit.note: Contain, cover, stretch, and none use Ghostty's full-pane fit equations, including padding; contain is the default and none maps one decoded pixel to one physical device pixel. Resize, DPR, and fit reload recompute placement without another decode or upload. Pure geometry plus the packed-RGBA RHI material are covered, including fractional DPR.

background-image-opacity.note: The exact finalized f32 defaults to 1 and remains an unclamped relative multiplier, including documented values above one. The packed-RGBA material uses the rounded global-background alpha: opaque source pixels reach min(global opacity times image opacity, 1), transparent pixels reveal the global background, and global opacity zero suppresses the image. Option-only reload updates pane composition without decoding or texture upload, and minimum contrast intentionally ignores image pixels. OpenGL/Vulkan RHI integration covers the material and retained one-texture upload telemetry; the separately planned alpha-blending modes are not claimed.

background-image-position.note: All nine full-pane anchors are implemented, with both center and center-center mapping to the middle. Each split has an independent origin, position reload performs no decode or texture upload, and right/bottom anchors retain negative offsets when a fitted image is larger than the pane. Pure placement and OpenGL-RHI material integration are covered.

background-image-repeat.note: The default-false boolean repeats the fitted tile in both axes before and after its pane-local anchor, and reload reuses the existing decoded image and texture. The public-QSG RHI material uses Ghostty's explicit positive modulo coordinates with a clamped linear texture, avoiding an ordinary repeated sampler's cross-seam filtering. Fractional-DPR hard-seam behavior passes RHI integration; the software scene-graph fallback retains its documented repeated-texture seam approximation.

background-opacity.note: The finalized f64 defaults to 1, is clamped to [0, 1], and reloads every existing and future split pane without replacing its scene root, session worker, terminal, or PTY. The pane base layer uses Ghostty's rounded 8-bit alpha. Qt requests an alpha-capable native surface before any window and the QML terminal host is transparent, while retained top or bottom chrome and the ordinary interactive split dividers remain opaque. Offscreen coverage verifies the Qt surface format, divider fallback, and emitted alpha values; final hardware/compositor output remains an interactive Wayland check.

background-opacity-cells.note: The exact default-false boolean preserves style and erase-cell explicit background provenance from the public libghostty render-cell query even when its RGB equals the terminal background. Explicit cell backgrounds are opaque when false and use Ghostty's truncated 8-bit background opacity when true; selection, candidate or selected search, and inverse backgrounds remain opaque, while default cells expose the rounded pane base. Minimum contrast composes the quantized linear-premultiplied cell layer over that base before evaluating glyphs and decorations. Reload is GUI-owned and pane-local.

bell-audio-path.note: The pinned parser finalizes relative paths and preserves required/optional provenance through the strict typed wire. With audio enabled, every pane lazily owns one reusable QMediaPlayer/QAudioOutput pipeline, rebuilds only for a changed identity or invalid medium, retries inaccessible paths on later bells, and keeps optional failures quiet.

bell-audio-volume.note: The raw finite f64 value is transported without premature normalization, applies live on the next BEL, and is clamped to zero through one only at the QAudioOutput playback boundary.

bell-features.note: The strict schema transports Ghostty's complete finalized system/audio/attention/title/border set. Every BEL independently calls Qt's best-effort public platform beep for system and replays the pane-local custom source for audio, while also latching its source pane and publishing an every-event GUI notification. Focus, non-modifier key or IME interaction, and any terminal mouse press clear that pane. Title prefixes only the active surface's displayed raw-derived tab/window title, border uses a three-pixel half-opacity input-transparent per-pane overlay, and attention requests QWindow's native indefinite alert only for an inactive host. Inactive tabs retain a separate stable attention marker until selected, including bells from non-active splits. All live changes apply to the next BEL without clearing the latch or changing pane/grid/PTY identity.

bold-color.note: The renderer implements Ghostty's unset, bright-palette, and fixed-color bold foreground rules while retaining palette/direct/default color provenance.

click-repeat-interval.note: The strict config projection carries Ghostty's finalized whole-millisecond value, including the Linux 500 ms default. Qt converts a nonzero arbitrary-origin millisecond window-system timestamp to nanoseconds with checked multiplication; zero or overflow produces an untimed press. The worker supplies the live interval and physical cell width, and libghostty accepts a repeat at inclusive consecutive-time and Euclidean-distance thresholds, with distance anchored to the original first press. It owns cell/word/line classification and clamps later repeats at triple; Linux Ctrl maps triple-click to OSC 133 semantic output while Meta/Super remains line. A Shift-left released by the effective mouse-shift-capture policy becomes an immediate drag only when a selection exists and its comparable timestamp is strictly more than the live interval after the retained ordinary press; the exact boundary remains an ordinary repeat candidate. The extension preserves libghostty's tracked anchor and selection behavior without replacing the retained press time, and Linux Ctrl+Alt selects rectangle mode for ordinary drags or delayed Shift extension. The pointer becomes a crosshair for Ctrl+Alt normally or Shift+Ctrl+Alt under raw DEC tracking, below hidden/link cursor priority. Qt ignores MouseButtonDblClick because its physical press already arrived. Reload affects the next press without reshaping an installed selection; ordinary release preserves repeat history, reported physical buttons reset it, and reported motion, wheels, or captured fractional scrolling preserve it.

class.note: The finalized optional raw value is resolved once before D-Bus arbitration or native surface creation. A valid GApplication/D-Bus application ID becomes both Qt's Wayland desktop-file identity and the single-instance service name; an invalid configured value emits a byte-exact diagnostic and falls back to the validated build application ID. Live reload deliberately cannot change this startup-only process identity.

clipboard-codepoint-map.note: Schema v1 preserves Ghostty's finalized ordered u21 ranges and codepoint-or-UTF-8 replacements, including empty deletion strings and non-scalar codepoints. SessionWorker applies the live list after plain selection formatting with Ghostty's last-overlapping-entry-wins rule, emitting U+FFFD for a non-scalar codepoint exactly like the pinned formatter. Explicit action/context copies, automatic primary/standard copies, and select_all share that worker-atomic path; title, URL, terminal-file, and search consumers remain unmapped. Status is partial because automatic and mixed copies still lack Ghostty's exact styled MIME payload and upstream must define mapping behavior for VT/HTML.

clipboard-paste-bracketed-safe.note: The live default-true policy trusts newlines only while Ghostty reports bracketed-paste mode, still rejects an embedded end fence, and shares one mode snapshot with encoding.

clipboard-paste-protection.note: The live default-true policy is enforced on SessionWorker. Unsafe immutable text is correlated through pane-local request IDs; confirmation re-snapshots mode, and rejected or cancelled requests do not scroll, write, or mark activity.

clipboard-read.note: Public libghostty-vt explicitly ignores OSC 52 clipboard-read requests instead of publishing them through the host callback. Exact Ghostty ask/allow/deny reads therefore require a new public normalized request contract; ghostty-qt does not add a parallel escape parser.

clipboard-trim-trailing-spaces.note: The current selection is formatted on the session thread through libghostty's plain formatter with the live trim option and soft-wrap unwrapping.

clipboard-write.note: The exact ask, allow, and deny values cross the strict config wire, default to allow, and reload live. Public libghostty-vt normalizes OSC 52 and OSC 1337 into ordered, owned, binary-safe requests; allow commits all MIME representations atomically, deny returns a denied result without queuing an effect or advertising DA1 feature 52, and ask advertises feature 52 but enters one bounded FIFO confirmation at a time. Standard maps only to Qt's standard clipboard, while selection and primary both map only to the available Linux selection clipboard. Stable PaneId validation discards exited or removed sources, the workspace retains at most 64 requests and 64 MiB, and an ask decision may be remembered for only its split until the next config reload.

command.note: The exact pinned parser supplies a nullable raw-byte shell/direct union. Shell values execute byte-for-byte through /bin/sh -c; direct values preserve the parser's literal-space argv boundaries and use the launching process PATH for bare argv[0] lookup before finalized env overrides are installed. The finalized default shell follows Ghostty's SHELL/passwd selection, and reload affects future panes.

command-palette-entry.note: Finalized title, description, action key, and canonical serialized action values populate each window-local Qt model after unsupported frontend actions are removed. On every palette opening they are combined with current typed surface-target rows, then prepared and deterministically sorted using colon-normalized case-insensitive keys. Filtering case-folds the query against cached keys for that row snapshot, equivalent replacement preserves selection by typed command identity, and configured actions close the modal before executing against the source window's then-current active pane.

config-default-files.note: The Ghostty CLI-only boolean is parsed with the pinned boolean grammar and forwarded to every private-helper query. False discards standard user configuration candidates before replaying explicit CLI/config-file sources; successful snapshots omit those candidates from the live watcher set while still retaining explicit recursive includes. A config-file occurrence intentionally cannot toggle the value, matching pinned Ghostty, and single-instance launch forwarding preserves an explicit startup override.

config-file.note: The pinned parser owns recursive include precedence and diagnostics. Existing include files, directories containing missing optional or required includes, atomic replacements, and failed-load retries all participate in asynchronous live reload while the last valid generation remains active.

confirm-close-surface.note: false, true, and always map to live workspace close policy. Linux PTY foreground groups and a command-submission latch cover ordinary jobs and pre-output races. Successful shell injection protects startup until its first OSC 133 prompt; public libghostty row/cell semantic metadata then distinguishes same-process-group shell builtins, alternate-screen work, and a returned prompt, while query failure remains active after integration is expected or observed. Status remains partial because the public API does not expose Ghostty's private live cursor semantic mode or a terminal-owned integration-seen bit; shells without installed integration retain the foreground/latch fallback.

copy-on-select.note: Linux false, primary-only true, and clipboard destination modes apply live, including standard fallback when primary selection is unavailable. Automatic copies use the same live trim and clipboard-codepoint-map path as explicit plain copies, but currently contain only plain text instead of Ghostty's mixed plain-plus-HTML payload; the missing exact public formatter contract is tracked in REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md.

cursor-click-to-move.note: Ghostty gates this feature on its private live semantic click mode and computes exact prompt-relative shell movement inside Surface. Official libghostty-vt exposes neither that mode nor the cursor-click movement operation; duplicating it from visible cells would diverge across wrapped prompts, continuations, and compressed scrollback.

cursor-color.note: The exact pinned parser supplies explicit colors and cell foreground/background aliases; live default updates preserve terminal OSC 12 overrides and OSC 112 reveals the newest configured default.

cursor-opacity.note: Configured cursor opacity is clamped and applied to the focused cursor; an unfocused cursor becomes Ghostty's opaque hollow outline.

cursor-style.note: Block, bar, underline, and hollow-block defaults apply to new and existing panes while terminal DECSCUSR state survives reload until reset.

cursor-style-blink.note: The configured default is applied, but public libghostty-vt exposes only a boolean setter and cannot preserve Ghostty's explicit true/false precedence over DEC mode 12.

cursor-text.note: Fixed, cell-foreground, and cell-background cursor text colors are resolved per rendered cursor cell with Ghostty's unset fallback.

custom-shader.note: Repeatable finalized required/optional paths preserve declaration order and empty-reset semantics. Sources up to 4 MiB are compiled asynchronously into validated SPIR-V, desktop GLSL, and GLES QSB variants; identical concurrent pane work coalesces and structurally validated outputs use a content-addressed disk cache, so same-path edits are detected without blocking the GUI or render thread. One physical-resolution Qt Quick source layer and a retained QRhi ping-pong executor apply the complete ordered chain to pane-local terminal and Kitty content through the pinned ShaderToy mainImage, iChannel0, cursor constants, bottom-left coordinates, and std140 uniform contract while leaving Qt chrome outside. The final pass renders inline and chains longer than two passes retain at most two intermediate textures. Missing optional files are skipped; any missing required file or invalid program disables the new chain and publishes a visible diagnostic, while a runtime retained-pipeline failure queues a pane-local fallback to direct unfiltered rendering and only retries retained rendering after a newer successful compile or scene-graph reset. Qt Quick's OpenGL or Vulkan RHI backend is required: other backends leave the terminal unfiltered and report that limitation, and final GPU/compositor presentation remains an interactive check.

custom-shader-animation.note: The pinned false, true, and always values map to never, focused, and always animation. Frame-swapped pacing advances time, delta, and frame while retained immutable snapshots carry the latest cursor, focus, palette, and color state. Updating an animated effect does not rebuild terminal cells or dirty retained row caches. Animation stops when policy, pane visibility, focus, window exposure, or backend support makes another frame unnecessary.

desktop-notifications.note: The standalone public libghostty-vt stream parses OSC 9 and OSC 777 but discards the normalized desktop-notification action. Exact frontend policy and delivery require a public effect callback; ghostty-qt does not parse PTY bytes a second time.

enquiry-response.note: The strict config projection preserves Ghostty's finalized raw bytes, including embedded NUL, and the empty default is silent. Every ENQ (0x05) invokes the public libghostty callback once; each non-empty response that fits the pinned callback's 255-byte payload boundary is returned byte-exactly through the terminal-generated PTY-write path, independently of read-only surface-input policy. Existing panes replace their adapter-owned response on live reload before later terminal parsing. The pinned public libghostty bridge silently drops payloads of 256 bytes or more even though full Ghostty's termio path has no corresponding configured-length limit; REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md tracks that remaining gap.

env.note: The private typed projection preserves Ghostty's finalized ordered raw-byte override map, including repeated-key replacement, configured-key removal, whole-map reset, and include precedence. Each pane snapshots the map at construction and applies it byte-exactly after inherited and terminal-injected values; a concrete working directory writes PWD last, while a configured PATH is visible to the child without changing parent-PATH executable lookup. Removal/reset do not unset inherited variables. Embedded NUL is rejected as an execve-safety hardening.

faint-opacity.note: Configured faint opacity applies to glyphs and text decorations without dimming cell backgrounds.

focus-follows-mouse.note: The exact default-false boolean reloads live per pane. Accepted hover and button-drag motion focuses an unfocused pane only while its existing Qt window is active, so an inactive host is never raised and retains its current focus item. The shared physical-pixel filter rejects synthetic same-position motion and accumulates subpixel movement against the last accepted position. Focus publication is guarded against synchronous pane or workspace destruction.

font-codepoint-map.note: The strict schema preserves finalized u21 ranges and family strings. GUI-thread resolution compiles overlaps in O(n log n) into sorted disjoint later-entry-wins intervals, including an unavailable latest face masking an older entry, and interns repeated resolved families in a compact face table. Cell lookup is logarithmic, always selects the mapped regular face, requires complete grapheme coverage, and ignores ZWJ plus text/emoji variation selectors for coverage. The immutable program is shared across panes and live reload replaces it without pane or PTY recreation. Status remains partial because public libghostty-vt does not expose Ghostty's resolved face collection, codepoint resolver, or face coverage decisions, so Qt owns platform discovery and glyph support.

font-family.note: Pinned parsing, exact CLI precedence, four-role propagation, live reload, and ordered Qt fallback families are implemented. Equal effective font inputs share one weak-cached immutable program across panes and DPRs, and Qt font-database changes invalidate every live pane's program. Status remains partial because Ghostty's embedded production fallback stack and resolver are not exposed through public libghostty-vt, so Qt's platform resolver supplies the final fallback behavior.

font-family-bold.note: The finalized ordered family list, role inheritance, synthesis permission, and live replacement are preserved. A disabled bold style uses the regular role, while a missing configured bold face may request Qt synthesis when permitted. Status remains partial because Qt owns final family substitution, fallback order, and native-versus-synthetic face selection.

font-family-bold-italic.note: The finalized ordered family list, role inheritance, synthesis permission, and live replacement are preserved. A disabled bold-italic style uses the regular role, while a missing configured combined face may request Qt synthesis when permitted. Status remains partial because Qt owns final family substitution, fallback order, and native-versus-synthetic face selection.

font-family-italic.note: The finalized ordered family list, role inheritance, synthesis permission, and live replacement are preserved. A disabled italic style uses the regular role, while a missing configured italic face may request Qt synthesis when permitted. Status remains partial because Qt owns final family substitution, fallback order, and native-versus-synthetic face selection.

font-feature.note: The pinned feature parser supplies the complete ordered list, including implicit defaults and duplicate tags; later tags overwrite earlier ones in Qt's shaping font while a feature such as pwid cannot alter the regular face's authoritative grid metrics. Compatible cells are shaped together, programming ligatures may retain non-grid internal caret positions when Qt reports a grid-aligned shaping cluster, and reload replaces the typography without pane, terminal, or PTY recreation. Malformed cluster metadata or a validated physical-grid mismatch retains exact per-cell fallback. Status remains partial because public libghostty-vt does not expose Ghostty's HarfBuzz feature application, selected faces, or positioned glyph plan, so QTextLayout owns the final shaping result.

font-shaping-break.note: The finalized cursor break flag reloads live. Maximal row runs break at font, foreground, complete style, selection, invisible cells, defensive plain fi/fl/st pairs, and optionally the logical cursor cell; wide spacers stay attached to their head. The renderer first validates every QTextLayout boundary in physical pixels. If only internal caret positions differ, it derives shaping clusters from Qt's glyph string indexes and instead validates cluster starts plus the run endpoint, permitting safe multi-cell programming ligatures. Incomplete or inconsistent cluster metadata and any validated grid mismatch fall back to exact per-cell placement for the run. Status remains partial because Ghostty's private run iterator and positioned glyph plan are not available through public libghostty-vt, so final cluster placement remains Qt-owned.

font-size.note: The pinned f32 value, exact CLI precedence, initial geometry, inheritance, and live reload are implemented. Manually adjusted panes retain their local size while adopting other typography changes; reset_font_size restores the newest live default and resumes following reloads.

font-style.note: Ghostty's automatic, disabled, and named alternatives cross the typed wire and reload live; pinned runtime semantics normalize disabled regular style to automatic. Status remains partial because Qt owns named-style substitution and final face selection rather than Ghostty's Fontconfig and FreeType collection.

font-style-bold.note: Ghostty's automatic, disabled, and named alternatives select the bold role and reload live. Disabled uses the regular role; a missing automatic or named role requests synthesis only when its permission is enabled. Status remains partial because Qt owns exact style matching and native-versus-synthetic face selection.

font-style-bold-italic.note: Ghostty's automatic, disabled, and named alternatives select the bold-italic role and reload live. Disabled uses the regular role; a missing automatic or named role requests synthesis only when its permission is enabled. Status remains partial because Qt owns exact style matching and native-versus-synthetic face selection.

font-style-italic.note: Ghostty's automatic, disabled, and named alternatives select the italic role and reload live. Disabled uses the regular role; a missing automatic or named role requests synthesis only when its permission is enabled. Status remains partial because Qt owns exact style matching and native-versus-synthetic face selection.

font-synthetic-style.note: The finalized bold, italic, and bold-italic synthesis permissions cross the typed schema and reload live. Native role faces are preferred; an allowed missing automatic or named styled role requests Qt synthesis, while a disabled permission or style uses the regular role. Status remains partial because Qt does not expose Ghostty's backend-specific FreeType synthetic-face construction or its exact bold and italic transforms.

font-thicken.note: Upstream implements stroke thickening only in its macOS CoreText renderer.

font-thicken-strength.note: This value only controls the macOS-only font-thicken renderer path.

font-variation.note: The finalized ordered regular-face axis list crosses schema v1 as exact f64 bit patterns, including non-finite values. The first matching tag is consumed before validity and range checks, matching the pinned FreeType duplicate policy, and valid axes reload live. Status remains partial because Qt narrows applied values to its float axis API and does not expose Ghostty's selected FreeType face and variation-coordinate pipeline.

font-variation-bold.note: The finalized bold-face variation list preserves exact f64 bits, order, and first-matching-tag semantics before Qt applies supported in-range axes. Final face selection and variation coordinates remain Qt-owned rather than Ghostty-owned.

font-variation-bold-italic.note: The finalized bold-italic-face variation list preserves exact f64 bits, order, and first-matching-tag semantics before Qt applies supported in-range axes. Final face selection and variation coordinates remain Qt-owned rather than Ghostty-owned.

font-variation-italic.note: The finalized italic-face variation list preserves exact f64 bits, order, and first-matching-tag semantics before Qt applies supported in-range axes. Final face selection and variation coordinates remain Qt-owned rather than Ghostty-owned.

foreground.note: The exact pinned parser supplies the color and the libghostty adapter applies it to new and existing panes.

freetype-load-flags.note: All five finalized booleans cross the strict typed schema and reload live. Qt maps disabled hinting, effective light versus full hinting, and monochrome antialias policy to public QFont controls. Force-autohint and autohint are transport-only no-ops and are excluded from the effective font-program cache key, as is light while hinting is disabled. Status remains partial because public Qt cannot request Ghostty's exact FreeType load flags or expose the resulting face options.

fullscreen.note: The exact pinned enum defaults false. True and every non-native variant map to Qt native fullscreen on Linux for each subsequently created window; reload never changes existing window state. When maximize is also true, action- and compositor-driven fullscreen exits restore maximized.

grapheme-width-method.note: The standalone public libghostty-vt constructor does not expose Ghostty's legacy versus Unicode grapheme-width policy for new terminals. Recomputing clusters in Qt would diverge from the terminal model and mode 2027 override.

input.note: The strict helper exports Ghostty's finalized ordered raw/path variants as lossless byte arrays. Before creating launch pipes or forking, SessionWorker resolves every path relative to the frontend process working directory, requires a regular readable file, and reads at most the exact 10 MiB limit; any failure aborts the entire pane without a child or cgroup move. Distinct chunks retain source order and are queued before started is published, so later GUI input cannot overtake them. Reload affects only subsequently constructed panes, including leaving an already deferred pane's immutable launch snapshot unchanged.

initial-command.note: The tagged command replaces ordinary command only for the first session that successfully initializes libghostty-vt. Suppressed startup, close-before-deferred-start, and terminal initialization failure preserve the process-wide FIFO lease; child-launch failure consumes it. Reload can replace the pending value before reservation, an existing holder keeps its immutable snapshot, and a consumed lease cannot be re-armed. Explicit `-e` or retained `--` CLI argv has first-pane precedence, and later surfaces use ordinary command.

initial-window.note: The exact default-true boolean is sampled once per launching process. False starts a primary with no QML root or surface and makes an occupied-name secondary exit successfully without activation; a fresh true launcher still activates that false-started primary. The installed D-Bus service explicitly starts a unique false-initial-window host, then its queued standard activation creates exactly one first surface. Explicit bootstrap CLI values outrank configuration and reload. Local/application/process/desktop creation remains unconditional. The first session that successfully initializes receives the current one-shot program and hold values. Construction or presentation failure before libghostty-vt initialization, terminal initialization failure, and closing a deferred root before start do not consume them; a later child-launch failure does. Later sessions use ordinary launch defaults, and reload alone creates or closes nothing. Following pinned GTK's executable requested-window guard, a process that has never created a surface stays resident; the documented initial-delay behavior is not reachable because GTK exposes no startup quit-timer hook.

image-storage-limit.note: The exact finalized u32 byte limit defaults to 320,000,000, initializes both libghostty screens, and applies live without recreating the pane or PTY. Zero disables and clears image storage. Ordinary Kitty placements use owned generation-stamped snapshots and retained Qt textures across all three z layers. A reverse render-order pass omits an older placement only after a successfully imported fully opaque placement at the same z and exact physical destination covers it, preserving libghostty state so later deletion can reveal the predecessor. Every asset retains one packed straight-alpha RGBA8 CPU image and one GPU texture; explicit raw RHI upload plus shader-time premultiplication preserves straight-alpha filtering while halving the former translucent two-plane footprint. Unicode virtual placements remain partial because public libghostty-vt does not expose their expanded viewport fragments. Renderer CPU/GPU mirrors remain additional to the configured Ghostty storage budget, and REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md records the pinned library's tracked-pin leak during image eviction and external-placement replacement.

keybind.note: A private versioned export carries Ghostty's finalized root and named-table bindings. Per-surface table stacks, shared-prefix sequences, physical/Unicode/catch-all triggers, chains, local flags, stage-time VT encoding, invalid replay, application-wide all/global dispatch, and Linux XDG portal registration are implemented for the supported action subset. Selection-dependent copy, search, endpoint adjustment, and viewport movement use correlated worker-authoritative performability across separate input events; local and broad chains wait for ordered GUI effects before continuing. Portal registration intentionally matches the pinned GTK frontend's root/direct/single-action restriction.

window-padding-y.note: The finalized u32 pair defaults to 2 points on both top and bottom and is snapshotted per pane, so reload affects only future windows, tabs, and splits. Linux converts each side to floor(points times DPR times 96/72) physical pixels. Initial cell-sized windows add the explicit margins, and the authoritative layout keeps renderer origin, hit testing, padding-excluded rows, libghostty surface geometry, and Ghostty's padding-excluded terminal PTY pixel extent coherent.

window-save-state.note: Upstream window restoration is macOS-only and explicitly has no effect on Linux.

window-show-tab-bar.note: The exact always/auto/never enum defaults to auto. Always shows the QML tab strip at every tab count, auto hides it for one tab and shows it at two or more, and never hides it; config reload and one/two-tab transitions update the property live. Acceptance covers workspace state and real QML visibility while the surrounding toolbar remains available.

window-step-resize.note: Discrete focused-cell window stepping is currently supported by upstream only on macOS.

window-subtitle.note: False and working-directory map to an optional client-toolbar subtitle. The value follows the selected tab's active stable pane, including OSC 7 directory changes, split focus, tab changes, tab removal, and live reload, without altering the exact native window title.

window-theme.note: Auto, system, light, dark, and ghostty are finalized by Ghostty and apply live. Auto and ghostty use Ghostty's AERT luminance threshold with only values strictly above 0.5 considered light; separate light/dark themes finalize auto to system. System tracks Qt's platform color-scheme signal. Resolved chrome remains opaque and updates existing windows without recreating panes or scene roots.

window-title-font-family.note: The optional non-monospace family applies live to the retained Qt toolbar, tab titles, controls, and subtitle. Unsetting restores the current Qt application font without changing terminal typography or grid geometry.

window-titlebar-background.note: In window-theme=ghostty, the optional color applies live to both top and bottom client chrome and otherwise falls back to the configured terminal background. Alpha is forced opaque; the setting is ignored in every other window-theme mode.

window-titlebar-foreground.note: In window-theme=ghostty, the optional color applies live to client-toolbar text and controls and otherwise falls back to the configured terminal foreground. Alpha is forced opaque; the setting is ignored in every other window-theme mode.

window-vsync.note: Ghostty currently supports this rendering synchronization option only on macOS.

window-width.note: The finalized u32 cell count participates only when paired with nonzero window-height. Every future window derives hidden normal geometry from its resolved Qt terminal font, inherits the live source/focused screen when available, includes construction-time explicit padding and declared QML chrome, applies a screen-bounded 10x4 cell minimum, and clamps best-effort before one activation-aware presentation; reload leaves existing windows unchanged. A normal first pane starts immediately from that viewport. Initially maximized/fullscreen windows keep synchronous pane/controller registration but defer first-session initialization until an exposed compositor-assigned viewport remains stable across two presented frames; inactive first tabs derive current geometry from their logical split tree, pending runtime, read-only, focus, and typed input operations retain controller-owned order until initialization, duplicate readiness events cannot restart the session, and close-before-exposure launches no child or process-derived confirmation. The resulting one-shot geometry initializes libghostty and forkpty before child exec; immediate ioctl probes confirm matching rows, columns, and padding-excluded terminal PTY pixels. Tabs, splits, bare-QML fallback initialization, and normal windows remain immediate and cannot inherit the window seed.

working-directory.note: The shared-config value supplies initial panes plus new-tab, split, and new-window fallback; explicit home/tilde paths, process-cwd and logical-PWD inherit behavior, symlink-sensitive concrete spelling, explicit Qt CLI precedence, live future-surface updates, composite source identity, and pinned stale-PWD/non-fatal-chdir fallback are tested. The helper always appears CLI-launched, so an unset GTK desktop default resolves to inherit rather than context-dependent home; lossless non-UTF-8 path transport remains incomplete.

activate_key_table.note: Decodes Ghostty's canonical action byte escapes and activates the exact named table in the current pane with duplicate-top and maximum-depth rules.

activate_key_table_once.note: Decodes Ghostty's canonical action byte escapes, activates the exact pane-local one-shot table, and pops it when the innermost table supplies a match.

adjust_selection.note: Adjusts the logical selection endpoint in every pinned direction and scrolls an endpoint outside the viewport back into view within one session-thread transaction. Absence is worker-authoritatively unperformed; correlated local and broad barriers prevent a stale GUI selection cache from changing performability or action order.

clear_screen.note: Ghostty's semantic clear is not an escape-sequence alias: it is inert on the alternate screen, clears selection and scrollback, distinguishes semantic prompts, clears Kitty graphics when appropriate, and conditionally writes form feed to the child. Official libghostty-vt exposes neither that composite operation nor a sufficient exact primitive set; the required public contract is tracked in REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md.

close_all_windows.note: Deprecated upstream and intentionally a no-op on Linux.

close_surface.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling and targets the originating stable PaneId plus its containing TabId. Local closure preserves an unrelated active pane, otherwise focuses the previous tree-order leaf except that the leftmost target selects the next leaf; it recursively collapses the split tree, clears only a removed zoom target, removes a final-leaf tab, and approves ordinary shutdown of only that pane's window after the final tab. Pinned GTK also selects the target's neighbor for an inactive programmatic close, whereas Qt deliberately preserves the unrelated active pane. Read-only/running confirmation uses correlated nonzero IDs, revalidates the stable target, and resolves plus commits atomically against synchronous topology observers; window-close approval permanently rejects later structural typed workspace actions so no worker can miss the shutdown sweep, while application-quit escalation and non-structural application or pane-local chain steps remain eligible to finish. Final closure then enters the application-owned last-window policy only if no other primary window remains. Real all:/global: bindings are consumed without PTY input and intentionally converge on one atomic confirmation/window close per Qt workspace. Pinned Ghostty instead fans broad actions to each surface in creation/swap-remove order: GTK closes safe leaves immediately and requests per-surface confirmation for unsafe leaves, while retaining only one pending split-close handle rather than independent stable requests. Full parity also remains limited by the separately tracked prompt-marker approximation.

close_tab.note: Accepts the exact omitted/this/other/right grammar through a typed mode, anchors to the originating pane's stable containing tab, treats valid no-target modes as performed, correlates dialog responses, and freezes TabId membership across confirmation, reordering, insertion, focus restoration, and overlapping worker shutdown. Commit traverses those frozen members in the then-current reverse visual order. Qt matches Ghostty macOS only in grouping a multi-tab close behind one atomic confirmation: macOS recomputes membership after confirmation and traverses ascending, while Qt retains the original membership. Pinned GTK instead confirms each unsafe target independently and immediately closes safe targets. Broad fanout also follows Qt's tab/tree snapshot order rather than Ghostty's surface creation/swap-remove order, while broad default/this retains the pre-existing single-workspace coalescing.

close_window.note: The exact void surface action requests ordinary closure of only the originating Qt window, aggregates that window's stable panes behind one confirmation, and starts all of its worker shutdowns concurrently. Non-final closure leaves process lifetime untouched; final closure enters the resident/immediate/delayed application policy. Broad fanout resolves unique registered workspaces so each window receives one close request.

copy_to_clipboard.note: Plain copy uses Ghostty's public selection formatter with live trailing-space trimming, then applies the finalized ordered clipboard-codepoint-map with last-overlap precedence before worker-atomic optional clearing. Selection presence and formatting are worker-authoritative even across separate input events. Correlated local chains commit the clipboard before continuing, while all/global chains prepare panes concurrently and commit in stable workspace/tab/tree order before advancing. The accepted mixed spelling currently emits this mapped plain text, while VT, HTML, and exact mixed formatting require clipboard-specific styled state not exposed by official libghostty-vt; the required contract is tracked in REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md.

copy_title_to_clipboard.note: Local behavior is exact: only the void spelling is accepted, and the originating pane's raw persistent surface override or optional base is copied synchronously and byte-for-QString exact to the standard clipboard. Absent/empty titles return false; tab overrides, zoom/fallback labels, primary, trimming, selection clearing, focus, and terminal selection are excluded. All/global last-writer order follows Qt's tab/tree traversal rather than Ghostty's creation/swap-remove surface vector. Qt also models a direct program name as presentation fallback where pinned Ghostty may initialize it as a copyable base title.

copy_url_to_clipboard.note: The exact void action copies the originating pane's currently accepted hyperlink destination byte-for-QString exact as the standard text/plain clipboard payload without QUrl normalization. This covers OSC 8 and the pinned default URL/path matcher; unavailable custom link definitions are tracked under the separate link configuration key. Malformed explicit destinations remain copyable even when Qt desktop-service activation rejects them.

csi.note: Restores the configured byte payload from Ghostty's canonical action format, queues it with the CSI introducer as one contiguous sequence on the worker thread, and scrolls the viewport to the active area.

cursor_key.note: The pinned Binding.Action parser deliberately returns InvalidAction for cursor_key before parsing any payload. Ghostty's finalized binding export can therefore never contain this action, and ghostty-qt rejects the omitted, empty, and normal/application serialized forms at the same boundary instead of inventing an unreachable frontend grammar.

decrease_font_size.note: Parses the required payload with Ghostty's f32 grammar, clamps the delta to 0..255 (including pinned NaN/infinity behavior), computes max(1, current-delta) in binary32, and marks each targeted pane manually adjusted even for an effective no-op.

end_key_sequence.note: Root and named-table sequences flush only their staged leaders. A normally consumed binding suppresses its terminating key, an explicitly unconsumed binding subsequently encodes that key, broad fanout flushes inactive-pane sequences, and an invocation without an active sequence is a successful no-op.

end_search.note: Stops the cooperative pane scan, clears its highlights, and hides the pane-local Qt overlay. The public libghostty-vt artifact omits Ghostty's xev-dependent search thread, so this uses the frontend search foundation.

equalize_splits.note: Equalizes the source tab with Ghostty's same-axis subtree weighting while preserving focus and split zoom.

esc.note: Restores the configured byte payload from Ghostty's canonical action format, queues it with the ESC introducer as one contiguous sequence on the worker thread, and scrolls the viewport to the active area.

goto_split.note: Supports wrapped tree-order previous/next traversal, wrapped spatial directions, and legacy top/bottom aliases. Successful navigation consults the live split-preserve-zoom policy: canonical navigation transfers an existing zoom to the destination, while the canonical no-navigation default clears it; failed navigation is inert.

goto_tab.note: Selects a one-based tab index, rejects zero or values outside Ghostty's c_int frontend range at execution, and clamps higher representable indices to the final tab.

goto_window.note: Accepts exactly previous/next while retaining Ghostty's surface scope, then relays typed requests to the process-owned window registry. Traversal starts at the active registered root or otherwise tests the first registration, follows Qt registration order with one wrap, skips active, hidden, close-committed, invalid, and active-pane-less roots, restores minimized destinations, requests activation synchronously, and focuses the destination's active pane. Guarded activation and focus support reentrant traversal and callback-scheduled retirement without retaining stale registry objects; final activation remains compositor-mediated on Wayland. All/global invokes the traversal once per visited surface, matching pinned action-major fanout. Pinned GTK traverses its toolkit top-level list, whose ordering is not a portable contract; Qt deliberately uses stable creation/registration order.

increase_font_size.note: Parses the required payload with Ghostty's f32 grammar, clamps the delta to 0..255 (including pinned NaN/infinity behavior), computes min(current+delta, 255) in binary32, and marks each targeted pane manually adjusted even for an effective no-op.

ignore.note: The exact app-scoped no-op suppresses press/repeat encoding even on unconsumed bindings, deliberately leaves the corresponding release unsuppressed, wins in the root pre-pass before active named tables, and preserves Ghostty's bare catch-all invalid-sequence drop. All/global executes once and retains the same special release behavior.

inspector.note: Accepts the exact toggle/show/hide grammar as an executable, pane-scoped frontend action and preserves the originating stable pane identity. A separate Qt-native window reports live surface geometry, font, pointer, process, cursor, viewport, mouse, keybinding, renderer, shader, Kitty-image, color, and palette state without an additional dependency. It does not yet provide Ghostty's retained keyboard and parsed terminal-I/O event streams or its inactive-screen, page-allocation, and cell internals, which are not exposed by the public libghostty-vt API.

jump_to_prompt.note: Official libghostty-vt does not expose Ghostty's prompt-delta viewport operation. The required public contract and acceptance evidence are tracked in REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md; ghostty-qt carries neither a Qt scrollback scan nor a local Ghostty patch.

last_tab.note: Selects the final tab, matching Ghostty's non-MRU semantics.

move_tab.note: Moves the source surface's tab by a signed cyclic offset while retaining stable tab identity and selection.

navigate_search.note: Supports exact previous/next grammar, cyclic newest-to-oldest navigation, selected-result highlighting, and off-viewport scrolling. Candidate highlights in older viewports can lag until the bottom-up scan reaches them; terminal-data mutation restarts that scan, and inactive-screen results are not preserved independently.

new_split.note: Supports left/right/up/down placement plus omitted and explicit auto. Auto uses the originating surface's effective pixel aspect, choosing right only when width is greater and down otherwise; every split focuses the new pane and clears split zoom.

new_tab.note: Local, QML, and broad triggers create and select a tab through the typed workspace, retain each original source pane for directory/font inheritance, and honor the live current/end insertion policy.

new_window.note: The exact void application action is routed above all workspaces and runs once for root, all, or global dispatch. Surface-originated requests retain the composite originating workspace and stable PaneId for working-directory/font inheritance; ordinary source-less Activate keeps the pinned focused-cwd/configured-font asymmetry. Standard org.freedesktop.Application ActivateAction and its org.gtk.Actions sibling accept exact new-window and new-window-command variants with typed parameters and one FIFO startup queue. The standard interface propagates creation failure after delayed dispatch, while the GTK void action acknowledges once its handler runs. A command request applies its decoded command, working-directory, and explicit-empty-capable persistent title only to the new window's first surface. That surface still resolves and consumes or releases the process-wide initial-session lease before its remote command wins; later tabs, splits, and windows retain ordinary launch policy. Every window remains a checked registration/presentation transaction and can recreate a resident zero-window process.

next_tab.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling, advances with wraparound from the containing window's currently selected tab even when invoked by an inactive source surface, and reports false when no distinct target exists. All/global applies once per stable pane in each workspace, so the net movement is the pane count modulo the tab count.

open_config.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling and routes one process-scoped request for local, root, all, or global dispatch, including with zero windows. Linux edit selection examines preferred XDG config.ghostty before legacy config, chooses the first non-empty file or otherwise the first existing empty file, recursively creates the preferred path when neither exists, and uses exclusive creation so contents and concurrent creators are preserved. The selected local-file URL is opened through Qt desktop services; preparation and launch failures are logged without falling through to PTY input. This is the GUI action, not the separately tracked +edit-config CLI contract.

paste_from_clipboard.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling and reads the standard clipboard on the GUI thread. A missing text MIME representation is not performed, an explicitly present empty text representation is performed without PTY bytes, and non-empty text uses the worker-owned bracketed-paste, unsafe-paste confirmation, read-only, and active-screen safety path. All/global reaches every pane.

paste_from_selection.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling and reads the Linux primary selection directly on the GUI thread, without the middle-click standard-clipboard fallback. Text MIME presence, explicit-empty behavior, worker paste safety, read-only filtering, and broad pane fanout match paste_from_clipboard; platforms without primary-selection support report the action unperformed.

previous_tab.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling, moves with wraparound from the containing window's currently selected tab even when invoked by an inactive source surface, and reports false when no distinct target exists. All/global applies once per stable pane in each workspace, so the net movement is the pane count modulo the tab count.

prompt_surface_title.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling and targets the originating stable PaneId. The field snapshots the raw non-empty surface override when present, otherwise the optional base title or empty text; tab overrides, zoom decoration, and Qt launch fallbacks are excluded. OK preserves non-empty text exactly as a persistent per-pane override, blank clears only that override, and Cancel is inert. OSC, set_surface_title, and reset retain the hidden base while an override masks it. Surface and tab prompts share one modal FIFO; all/global enqueues once per pane, removed targets are resolved or pruned, and stale completions are inert.

prompt_tab_title.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling with no colon and targets the source surface's tab by stable identity. Each request snapshots the raw override when present or the current display title otherwise, including the modeled zoom prefix; the focused field places its caret at the end without selecting all. OK preserves text exactly, blank clears the override, and Cancel is inert. Requests share one FIFO with surface-title prompts, with all/global retaining one request per surface and no split-tab deduplication. Source-pane removal is harmless while its tab survives; target deletion resolves or prunes its requests, and stale completions cannot rename another tab.

quit.note: The exact void action is process-scoped and available with zero windows. It snapshots every live workspace before mutation, lets a safe active window host one confirmation when an inactive pane is running or read-only, leaves every window untouched on cancellation, then starts every workspace's worker shutdown before committing one irreversible process quit. It bypasses disabled/delayed last-window policy, handles an already approved host, rehosts if the dialog workspace disappears, and remains idempotent after commitment.

redo.note: Pinned Ghostty implements redo only on macOS; the Linux GTK application explicitly leaves it unimplemented.

reload_config.note: The process-scoped exact void action requests one debounced asynchronous reload of both configuration domains even with zero windows. A successful post-startup snapshot updates process keybindings, lifetime, every live workspace, and the defaults consumed by future windows, then publishes the configured window-local success toast. A hard failure retains the last valid state and presents source-labelled process diagnostics with retry and window-local ignore behavior.

reset.note: Performs libghostty's full terminal reset on the session thread, resynchronizes cached mouse-input, selection, and working-directory state, preserves the frontend's last published base title because upstream emits no application title update, and publishes a complete replacement frame without writing to the PTY.

reset_font_size.note: Rejects every parameter, restores the pane's newest configured font size without an action clamp, and clears manual adjustment so later live reloads apply. A fresh split uses its inherited effective size as this target until reload replaces it.

resize_split.note: Moves the nearest matching-axis ancestor divider by the requested pixel amount, clamps its ratio, and preserves focus and zoom.

scroll_page_down.note: Scrolls down by exactly the pane's full terminal row count.

scroll_page_fractional.note: Uses the pane's full row count with f32 multiplication and truncation toward zero; non-finite or unsafe values are rejected instead of reproducing the pinned frontend's conversion crash.

scroll_page_lines.note: Scrolls by the signed i16 line count with Ghostty's boundary clamping.

scroll_page_up.note: Scrolls up by exactly the pane's full terminal row count.

scroll_to_bottom.note: Pins the viewport to the active area through libghostty's tagged viewport API.

scroll_to_row.note: Scrolls to a usize absolute row in libghostty's full-screen/scrollbar coordinate space with terminal-side clamping.

scroll_to_selection.note: Normalizes the current selection to its visual top-left row and aligns that row to the viewport; absence remains non-performable. The session worker decides that state at execution and returns a correlated result, so local performable keys and process-wide chains do not consult an asynchronously reconciled GUI cache.

scroll_to_top.note: Pins the viewport to the top of scrollback through libghostty's tagged viewport API.

search.note: Replaces the literal needle without changing search-UI visibility, and an empty needle stops matching while leaving the overlay alone. The generation-cancelled bottom-up scan uses public grid references, whose reads temporarily restore compressed pages and therefore interleave bounded recompression. Flat public rows cannot exactly reproduce internal page-boundary delimiters or every blank-cell point mapping; mutations restart the scan, older viewport highlights can lag, and only the active screen has results.

search_selection.note: When a terminal selection exists, its exact untrimmed text becomes the needle and opens the pane overlay; a valid empty selection opens and focuses while retaining the previous entry text, matching pinned GTK sequencing. Without a selection the worker-authoritative correlated action is not performed. Local and broad chains commit the ordered overlay effect before continuing; search execution uses the cooperative frontend foundation.

select_all.note: Installs Ghostty's full selectable-content range and prepares the configured automatic clipboard copy from the same session-thread transaction. Its correlated result suspends local chains and process-wide action-major fanout until the GUI clipboard effect commits; broad effects publish in stable workspace/tab/tree order. The remaining exact mixed plain-plus-HTML automatic-copy payload limitation is tracked by copy_to_clipboard and REQUIRES_UPSTREAM.md.

set_font_size.note: Parses the required payload directly to f32, applies Ghostty's 1..255 clamp including NaN and signed-infinity behavior, and marks every targeted pane manually adjusted even when its effective size is unchanged.

set_surface_title.note: Requires a colon, decodes Ghostty's canonical escaped-byte transport as valid UTF-8, and replaces the originating stable pane's base title without changing focus or selection. An empty payload remains explicitly present rather than selecting the Qt fallback; later OSC metadata replaces it, including restoration of the exact pre-action cached string. Reset preserves the current base title regardless of its latest writer because pinned Ghostty publishes no application title update. Per-tab overrides continue masking base updates, and all/global applies once to every pane.

set_tab_title.note: Decodes Ghostty's canonical byte-string escapes and valid UTF-8, then applies a non-empty override to the source surface's tab by stable identity. An empty payload clears the override and reveals the active pane's effective surface title; focus and surface/base-title changes plus tab insertion and reordering preserve the override.

show_on_screen_keyboard.note: The exact void action validates its originating stable PaneId, focuses that pane without changing topology, and asks Qt's platform input method to show the on-screen keyboard.

start_search.note: Opens and focuses a pane-local Qt overlay, retaining and selecting its prior text without starting work for an empty needle. A non-focusing grip drags within the pane and snaps independently to the nearest corner for each pane. Status remains partial because the upstream xev-dependent search thread is unavailable in libghostty-vt.

text.note: Decodes the pinned Zig string-literal escape grammar on the session thread, preserves Unicode and embedded NUL bytes, writes without key encoding, and consumes malformed literals without PTY output.

toggle_command_palette.note: The exact void action toggles one retained modal per originating window with live custom entries, keyboard navigation, title/action-key filtering, deterministic Ghostty-style sorting, and close-before-action execution. Immediately before each open it adds one focus row for every committed live surface across normal and retained hidden quick-terminal windows, tabs, and splits. Rows preserve missing versus explicit-empty effective titles, suppress a cwd description only when the case-sensitive effective title already contains it, and carry a typed stable WindowId plus workspace-local PaneId rather than a QML string or pointer. Activation revalidates the composite target after closing, selects its exact tab and split, restores minimized or hidden presentation, and is inert after either the pane or whole window becomes stale.

toggle_fullscreen.note: Routes the finalized surface action through the typed workspace pipeline to toggle the containing Qt window; broad all/global fanout applies one transition per workspace, and Ghostty's Linux Ctrl+physical Enter default is active.

toggle_maximize.note: Routes the exact void surface action to maximize or restore the containing Qt window. Broad all/global fanout is intentionally coalesced once per workspace instead of reproducing pinned GTK's cancel-prone per-surface toggles; separate windows transition independently. Prior visibility, including maximized or minimized state, survives fullscreen round trips, and toggling maximize while fullscreen changes the eventual restore state without leaving fullscreen. Ghostty provides no default binding.

toggle_mouse_reporting.note: Flips the source pane's mouse-reporting policy without mutating terminal DEC mode. Effective capture is the per-event conjunction of both states; all/global toggles every stable pane once, each pane remains independent, and live reload restores configuration.

toggle_readonly.note: Toggles read-only state per source surface, including stable all/global fanout. Worker-ordered policy suppresses surface-originated key, IME, mouse-report, paste, and raw-action bytes while output, terminal-generated protocol replies, focus bookkeeping, and terminal-local selection, copy, search, and native scrolling remain active; toggling off resumes input without replay. An input-transparent top-right Read-only badge and active-pane model role publish the state. Read-only forces pane, tab, and workspace close confirmation regardless of confirm-close-surface, foreground activity, or child-exit state.

toggle_quick_terminal.note: The application action creates at most one layer-shell window, installs the Qt-owned layer and namespace before its first native presentation, injects exactly GHOSTTY_QUICK_TERMINAL=1 into that window's pane launch environment, forces compositor-owned frameless/deferred geometry, and then retains the same tabs, splits, PTYs, and UI controller across hide/show cycles. Shell-only reloads synchronize live without recompiling keybindings or walking terminal panes; quick-terminal tabs retain a tab strip while ordinary header chrome remains hidden.

toggle_split_zoom.note: Zooms the active leaf without rebuilding the tree or PTY sessions and publishes the zoom state to the tab strip.

toggle_tab_overview.note: The exact void action toggles a window-local modal grid backed by the live tab model. Activation closes the modal first and then resolves the selected stable TabId, so reordering or removal cannot target a different tab.

toggle_window_decorations.note: Accepts only the exact void spelling and requires a source surface attached to a host window. The first invocation installs the opposite none-versus-decorated override from the current configuration; the second clears that override and reveals the latest reloaded value. Local targets change only their containing window, while all/global fanout coalesces exactly once per workspace so multiple panes cannot cancel the toggle. The Qt projection mutates only FramelessWindowHint and leaves window state, geometry, unrelated flags, panes, and terminal workers intact. On Wayland, clearing the hint on an existing native surface restores Qt client-side framing instead of renegotiating prior compositor-side decoration; exact restoration requires native-surface recreation or private Qt APIs.

unbind.note: Implemented at configuration finalization by the pinned Ghostty helper: it removes the target binding before the structured trie reaches Qt. The directive is intentionally absent from the runtime action catalog and cannot execute or appear in a finalized action chain.

undo.note: Pinned Ghostty implements undo only on macOS; the Linux GTK application explicitly leaves it unimplemented.

write_screen_file.note: Accepts the required copy, paste, or open disposition with omitted or explicit plain format and consumes valid no-data invocations. It formats the complete active PageList with soft wraps removed, trailing spaces retained, and trailing blank rows dropped: primary includes history plus screen, while alternate contains only its own page. The persistent screen.txt artifact is mode 0600 inside a deliberately stricter mode-0700 temporary directory; pinned Ghostty leaves the directory at its umask-derived default. Copy publishes the absolute path as standard-clipboard text, paste writes its raw filesystem bytes without newline, quoting, or bracketed-paste framing, and open uses the desktop local-file handler. Correlated completion suspends a local chain until its GUI effect commits; all/global actions prepare every pane concurrently, then commit in stable workspace/tab/tree order before the next entry. Styled VT and HTML formats are recognized but remain unsupported: libghostty-vt's public terminal formatter can emit styled content, but its C options do not expose the exact effective foreground, background, and palette path used by the pinned ScreenFormatter action, so byte-compatible parity still needs a bridge or an explicitly validated equivalent.

write_scrollback_file.note: Implements the same correlated plain copy, paste, and open pipeline as write_screen_file but formats only primary-screen history into history.txt; alternate-screen use and an empty history are performed no-ops with no artifact. Successful files persist as mode 0600 under a mode-0700 directory instead of pinned Ghostty's umask-derived directory mode. Styled VT and HTML output remains unsupported until the public terminal formatter is bridged to or validated against the pinned ScreenFormatter color options.

write_selection_file.note: Implements the same correlated plain copy, paste, and open pipeline as write_screen_file for the current active selection, preserving inclusive endpoints and rectangular shape in selection.txt; no selection is a performed no-op with no artifact. Successful files persist as mode 0600 under a mode-0700 directory instead of pinned Ghostty's umask-derived directory mode. Styled VT and HTML output remains unsupported until the public terminal formatter is bridged to or validated against the pinned ScreenFormatter color options.

edit-config.note: Delegates the pinned Linux implementation before Qt starts: standard config loading and preferred-file creation, non-empty VISUAL then EDITOR selection, preferred/non-empty legacy path choice, shell-escaped path construction, /bin/sh replacement, raw streams, and editor exit status are preserved. The pinned implementation currently leaves a newly created file empty despite its template-writing intent. This is distinct from the GUI open_config action.

explain-config.note: Delegates the pinned implementation through the relocatable embedded-runtime helper before Qt starts.

help.note: The pinned +help implementation is delegated; the frontend's ordinary --help remains separate, and the printed upstream catalog is not a support claim for every listed action.

list-actions.note: Delegates the pinned action catalog through the relocatable embedded-runtime helper before Qt starts.

list-colors.note: Delegates the pinned color catalog and its action-specific options before Qt starts.

list-fonts.note: Delegates the pinned Linux implementation before Qt starts. The isolated helper is built with Ghostty's fontconfig_freetype backend, so family/style/bold/italic querying and prioritization, Fontconfig priority ordering for a requested family, and sorted unfiltered output use the exact upstream discovery path. This inventories the helper's Ghostty font stack; Qt still owns terminal shaping and fallback.

list-keybinds.note: Delegates the pinned finalized keybinding formatter through the embedded-runtime helper.

list-themes.note: Delegates the pinned implementation before Qt starts, preserving its path/plain/color options, non-TTY plain output, interactive TTY selector, ordering, streams, and exit status. Zig emits the pinned bundled themes into a relocatable helper-only resource tree; a non-empty GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR remains authoritative, otherwise the helper discovers build and installed resources relative to /proc/self/exe. Standard user themes remain under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ghostty/themes. Deterministic tests cover bundled and user listings, filtering, paths, explicit overrides, and moved-prefix discovery. Qt terminal rendering and fallback remain independent.

new-window.note: Before any GUI startup, the raw-argv client reproduces pinned Ghostty's class targeting, concrete cwd tilde/relative realpath normalization, implicit caller-cwd insertion, home/inherit forwarding quirk, opaque arguments after `-e`, UTF-8 validation, and exact org.gtk.Actions new-window-command string-array variant with empty platform data. It performs one blocking D-Bus call with service activation and no retry or local fallback. The primary decodes last-valid command/cwd/title values, including Ghostty's literal relative-path treatment of winning home/inherit values, unknown-option ignoring, direct/shell command grammar, and non-empty argv-after-`-e` precedence; overrides apply only to the registered first surface while preserving the global initial-session lease lifecycle. Warm and cold private-bus process tests cover the real executable path.

show-config.note: Delegates the pinned implementation through ghostty-qt's app-runtime=none helper; GTK-runtime-specific finalization is intentionally outside this embedded helper contract.

show-face.note: Delegates the pinned implementation before Qt starts. Codepoint/string, regular/bold/italic/bold-italic style, text/emoji presentation, and ordinary font configuration arguments use Ghostty's exact Fontconfig+FreeType resolver. This reports the isolated helper's face selection; Qt continues to own terminal shaping and fallback. The pinned revision writes action parsing and resolution errors to stdout, and delegation intentionally preserves that stream quirk.

ssh.note: Delegates the pinned +ssh wrapper through the relocatable embedded-runtime helper before Qt starts. Ghostty owns wrapper-option parsing, destination resolution, exact wrapped-SSH arguments and streams, TERM and SendEnv forwarding, encoded xterm-ghostty installation and fallback, standard XDG-state cache integration, and child exit or signal-status mapping. Tests cover the action boundary, binary streams, environment and cwd inheritance, arbitrary exit and signal status, install failure, successful upload, cache write, and cached install suppression without network access. Automatic Bash, Elvish, Fish, Nushell, and Zsh wrappers invoke this same action through the staged shell-integration resources.

ssh-cache.note: Delegates the pinned +ssh-cache manager through the relocatable embedded-runtime helper before Qt starts. Ghostty owns the standard XDG-state path, list, exact and bare-host query, add/update, remove, prune, and clear grammar, validation, 0600 repair, atomic on-disk updates, streams, and exit status. Tests use an isolated repository-local state directory; no Qt cache namespace or frontend reimplementation is introduced.

toggle-quick-terminal.note: The pre-Qt raw-argv client invokes exact org.gtk.Actions toggle-quick-terminal on the default application identity with empty platform data, performs one blocking call with D-Bus service activation, and never falls back locally. Matching the pinned revision's executable behavior, every extra argument, including --class, is ignored. The primary toggles its single retained compositor layer surface with live quick-terminal policy and no pane or PTY recreation; the separate standard ActivateAction path can carry desktop activation context. Warm and cold process tests exercise the real client and service.

validate-config.note: Delegates the pinned validation implementation with raw arguments, streams, and exit status preserved.

version.note: Delegates the pinned detailed version report through the relocatable helper before Qt starts. It reports the exact Ghostty revision and release channel; its Zig mode, app-runtime=none, Fontconfig+FreeType backend, OpenGL renderer type, and libxev backend describe the embedded helper build, not ghostty-qt's Qt runtime or renderer. The frontend's ordinary --version remains a separate concise ghostty-qt version.
